title: Death of Herod the Great (4 BCE traditional; 1 BCE minority view)
summary: Herod the Great, king of Judea, died after a last illness, with Josephus placing his death between a lunar eclipse and the following Passover and the final scenes at Jericho. Most scholars date this to 4 BCE, linked to the eclipse of March 4 BCE; a minority argue for 1 BCE. The date sets a limit for dating the birth of Jesus.

uncertainty.note: Traditional date 4 BCE = astronomical -3. The minority 1 BCE view (astronomical 0) rests on a different lunar eclipse (10 January or 29 December, 1 BCE) and on Herod's sons backdating their reigns; a 3 BCE proposal also exists. The range runs from -3 to 0.

as_recorded.value: lunar eclipse of March 13, 4 B.C., traditionally associated with Josephus's account of Herod's death
Herod most likely died shortly after the lunar eclipse of December 29, 1 B.C. (minority view argued in a published letter)

where.modern_name: Jericho, West Bank (Herod's winter residence lay just southwest of the modern town)
where.historical_name: Jericho, in Herod's kingdom of Judea

importance.justification: The end of a major client-king reign in Judea; its disputed date fixes the latest limit for the traditional birth date of Jesus.

reviewer_note: Least sure of which date to treat as primary: 4 BCE is the conventional scholarly dating, 1 BCE is a minority view. Burial at Herodium was not confirmed on an opened page and is not claimed.
